Measures whether Face to Face Games slows this phone down. Prices a fixed list of real cards (%1$d) on facetofacegames.com at the scanner\'s own pacing — once over Cronet (Chrome\'s network stack) and once over plain OkHttp — and counts 429 “too many requests” answers. About 1–3 minutes per run. The store limits per internet address, so run it on the network the phone will price from, and don\'t price on the computer at the same time. Nothing is saved or sent anywhere; tap Copy results and paste them back.
Cooldown before %3$s — %1$d:%2$02d (the store\'s limit is per address)

The phone is your scanner\'s server: it identifies and prices every card and keeps the scans. A computer on the same Wi-Fi (or the phone\'s hotspot) can open them at the address below — pair it once as admin to delete, clear and export there. Anyone using the 6-digit code is a guest who can review and flag cards for deletion.
Not serving right now — it starts again when you open the app.
Serving, but the phone has no Wi-Fi address — join Wi-Fi or turn on the hotspot.

On the computer, open this address (or scan the code with its camera):

%1$s

or type this one-time code on the join page: %2$s

It works once, for 10 minutes. The computer is then remembered as the admin: it can delete, clear, export and run pricing. Anyone using the 6-digit code is a guest: they can review, pick and flag cards for deletion.

Pair on a network you trust (your home Wi-Fi or the phone's own hotspot): the connection is plain HTTP, so someone else on the same network could copy the admin cookie.
The server isn\'t reachable on a network yet — join Wi-Fi or turn on the hotspot, then try again.
Stop treating every paired computer as admin? They will need a new one-time code.
No card database yet — it downloads when the phone has internet. Scans wait until it\'s in.
